reviews.title: Beautiful Case With a Classic Wood Design and Great Functionality
reviews.comment: I used this case for my custom PC build and I absolutely love it. What originally drew me to it was the design. The wood front immediately reminded me of my dad’s old stereo cabinet, and that warm brown wood detail gives the case a very clean and classic look that stands out from typical gaming cases. Beyond the looks, the build experience was excellent. I was able to fit an AIO cooler and a full sized graphics card with no issues at all. There was plenty of room to work in, and everything felt well thought out during installation. The case also has a lot of great features that make building and maintaining a system easier. Airflow is solid, cable management is straightforward, and the overall construction feels sturdy and high quality. It manages to look stylish without sacrificing performance or practicality. If you want a case that combines modern PC functionality with a timeless design, this one is an excellent choice. It looks great in a room and performs just as well as it looks.
reviews.author: Jakari Jones

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment: I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build. The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to. The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk. Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore. Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity. I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case. If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation. Fractal nailed it. 🔥
reviews.author: Luke McKinnon

reviews.title: A premium quality case with great features and lots of room.
reviews.comment: I needed a good size case with lots of room for a work machine running a I-9 Core 285k with a Nvidia 5070ti. This case is very roomy and is very easy to use without cutting your hands up. The airflow is excellent with my temps well within expected ranges. It isn't cheap but you get what you pay for. Everything feels solidly built and very premium. While it wasn't a big consideration for me, if you like a mid century modern design, this case has a beautiful look that appears like a piece of fine furniture.
reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment: I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet. I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive. What I loved - Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines - Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included - Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters - Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio - Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear - Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards - Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained What could be better - Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further - Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped - Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit - No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly - Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs - Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying - Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance - Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier - Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches Verdict The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.
reviews.author: showmestuff

reviews.title: A great looking case that also cools well.
reviews.comment: I've been a Fractal Design fan for many years.  This one caught my eye when it was released.  I like the wood slats on the front.  They make it look more luxurious.  It has typical Fractal build quality.  That is to say it is excellent.  Building the system is easy.  Components fit exactly as they should.  Fractal's approach for air filters works well.  They are easy to clean.  I generally just run water over them in the sink and then dry them off.  The whole system is reasonably quiet.  Cable routing works well.  I've never been great at making the cables look professional but with this, it still looks good.  There are convenient Velcro strips to help. I do have three suggestions: - There should be a DIN plug for connecting all the front panel connections. - I miss having an LED to indicate drive activity. - They should make more of this model with a solid side panel.  I would prefer that over the glass side panel.  I don't really need to see inside the machine but would prefer the increased sound isolation an insulated, solid panel could provide.
reviews.author: Darrin J. Fangman
